sections.overview: The Ring Ouzel breeds in uplands across Europe and Central Asia, then winters farther south.
sections.identification: The male is dark with a bold white breast band; the female is browner, with a duller band.
sections.habitat: It breeds in open upland valleys and slopes, often among heather.
sections.diet: It eats invertebrates, including earthworms and beetles, and also takes berries.
sections.behavior: British birds leave after breeding and return from Africa in spring.
sections.reproduction: It nests on or near the ground, often in heather; a second brood may occur.
sections.ecology: Unlike the winter-visiting Fieldfare, it breeds in Britain in summer; see that profile for the contrast.
sections.conservation: It is on the UK Red List after long-term declines in breeding numbers and range.
